title: DTM median gridding on measured cells at 1 m cells, origin at the data minimum, against R terra
question: Does rasterizeDtm with median aggregation, deriving its own grid at 1 m cells from the data minimum, give the same per-cell median as R terra on the same points and grid, for cells that hold at least one return?

metrics.toleranceUnit: metre (OLV float32 against the reference rounded to float32)

claims.toleranceDerivation: Both sides take the median of the same returns, so the only expected difference is float32 storage on the OLV side. Rounding the reference to float32 removes that, and 1e-6 m then separates a last-bit difference from a different median. Every cell must pass and the occupancy masks must match exactly.

freeze.witness: The commit that adds validation/protocols/dtm-median-gridding-v3.md, which adds this parameter set to protocol v2 and keeps its references, datasets, input shift, grid rule, edge rule and tolerance, and fixes its minimum cell count, before any reference grid for these parameter sets existed.

decisionRule: Agree only when every compared cell is within 1e-6 m after rounding the reference to float32, the occupancy masks match exactly, at least 15000 cells are compared, and the two references (SciPy and R terra) agree with each other under the same rule. Otherwise report the failure with its numbers; the tolerance is never widened.
notes: Transcribes validation/protocols/dtm-median-gridding-v3.md, committed in the witness commit before any reference grid for this parameter set existed. It does not create that freeze.
terra builds the grid from the extent and resolution and does its own point-to-cell assignment and median. The fixtures and the comparison harness are this project's own.
